title: Deep Weakly-supervised Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Anomaly detection methods need to detect both labeled anomaly types seen during training and new anomaly types unseen during training.

gap.claim: Existing semi-supervised methods often fit only the abnormalities represented by the provided anomaly examples and fail to generalize to unseen anomaly types or classes.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces PReNet, a deep weakly-supervised approach that learns pairwise relation features and anomaly scores by predicting relations between randomly sampled training instances.
PReNet jointly learns anomaly-anomaly, anomaly-normal, and normal-normal pairwise discriminative patterns from labeled anomaly and mostly normal unlabeled data.
The pairwise approach augments the training anomaly data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe PReNet as a novel deep weakly-supervised approach for detecting seen and unseen anomalies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On 12 real-world datasets, PReNet significantly outperforms nine competing methods for detecting seen and unseen anomalies.
The authors theoretically and empirically justify model robustness to anomaly contamination in the unlabeled data.
Code is reported as available in the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Semi-supervised anomaly detection using few labeled anomalies and substantial unlabeled data improves over unsupervised methods.
These methods may fail to generalize beyond anomaly types represented in the labeled examples.
PReNet predicts pairwise relations among randomly sampled instances to learn relation features and anomaly scores.
The learned pairwise patterns support detection of seen and unseen abnormalities and augment anomaly training data.
The authors report comparative results across 12 datasets, robustness analysis under unlabeled-data contamination, and code availability.

source_observation.claim: The approach learns relations among anomaly-anomaly, anomaly-normal, and normal-normal instance pairs.

interpretation.claim: Relational supervision may provide broader anomaly structure than modeling only the labeled anomaly examples.

application.claim: For weakly supervised detection with few labeled anomalies, consider training objectives that include pairwise relations involving labeled and unlabeled instances.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when pairwise relations are reliable beyond the reported setting or how performance changes with different contamination levels.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, or identities of the nine competing methods.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, or pairwise relation labels in operational detail.
The abstract does not quantify the reported performance gains or robustness under anomaly contamination.
The abstract does not state limitations or conditions under which unseen anomalies may not fit learned abnormal patterns.
